blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Serious work on inclusion and equity requires a willingness to engage with complexity. The terminology itself has become contested; well-intentioned organisations routinely find themselves criticised both for doing too much and for doing too little, often by different stakeholders in the same week.

What tends to endure through the noise is a disciplined focus on outcomes rather than intentions. Do people from underrepresented groups progress at the same rate as others? Is there statistical evidence of unequal access to opportunity? Are decisions about hiring, pay and promotion consistent when examined closely? These are uncomfortable questions, but they are the right ones.

Equally important is the recognition that inclusion cannot be imposed through compliance alone. Policies set the floor; they do not set the ceiling. Real inclusion is built one conversation, one meeting, one decision at a time, and it is almost always led by managers — not by central HR initiatives.

items.q: According to the text, what tends to endure through the noise around inclusion?
options: The volume of policies an organisation publishes
A commitment to updating the terminology every year
The reputation of the central HR function
A disciplined focus on outcomes rather than intentions
items.why: "What tends to endure through the noise is a disciplined focus on outcomes rather than intentions."

items.q: What does the text say policies can and cannot do?
options: They replace the need for managers
They set the floor but not the ceiling
They set both the floor and the ceiling
items.why: "Policies set the floor; they do not set the ceiling."

items.q: The author suggests that the three questions about hiring, pay and promotion are "the right ones" mainly because they…
options: measure outcomes rather than good intentions
can be answered by central HR alone
are easy for stakeholders to agree on
items.why: Inferência: as perguntas medem progressão, acesso e consistência — ou seja, resultados, não intenções.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Managers are central to building real inclusion.
Once the right policy is signed off, inclusion is effectively achieved.
Uncomfortable questions about equity are worth asking.
Contested terms should be handled with precision.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que compliance é só o piso e que inclusão real se constrói decisão a decisão — não termina com uma política.

items.q: The fact that organisations are criticised "for doing too much and for doing too little… in the same week" suggests that…
options: the organisations are ignoring the data
the topic is unimportant to most people
the criticism proves the organisations are failing
items.why: Inferência: críticas opostas na mesma semana indicam expectativas divergentes entre stakeholders, não um veredito único.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando a auditoria de equidade ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before we get to the recommendations, I want to be candid about what three years of data show, because we owe each other precision rather than reassurance.

Promotion rates are not consistent across groups. Once you control for tenure and performance rating, colleagues from underrepresented groups are progressing at roughly two-thirds of the rate of their peers. That is a disparity, and I am not going to soften it. It is not explained by qualifications, and not by attrition.

I know some of you will want a single headline number and a policy to fix it. I would push back on that gently. A policy sets the floor; it does not close a gap like this. The evidence points to the everyday decision — who gets the visible project, who gets the benefit of the doubt in a calibration meeting. Those decisions sit with line managers, not with my team.

So my proposal is uncomfortable but honest. We publish these figures internally, we hold managers accountable for their own promotion outcomes, and we come back in twelve months to check whether the needle has actually moved.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does the data show once tenure and performance rating are controlled for?
options: The sample was too small to draw conclusions
Underrepresented colleagues progress at about two-thirds the rate of their peers
Underrepresented colleagues progress faster than their peers
Promotion rates are essentially equal across groups
items.why: "colleagues from underrepresented groups are progressing at roughly two-thirds of the rate of their peers."

items.q: How does Sophie respond to those who want "a single headline number and a policy to fix it"?
options: She says the problem is entirely about attrition
She agrees a policy will close the gap
She gently pushes back, saying a policy only sets the floor
She refuses to share any numbers
items.why: "I would push back on that gently. A policy sets the floor; it does not close a gap like this."

items.q: According to Sophie, where do the decisive everyday decisions sit?
items.why: "Those decisions sit with line managers, not with my team."

items.q: What does Sophie mean when she says she owes the board "precision rather than reassurance"?
options: She will only report good news
She will present an honest, exact picture even if it is uncomfortable
She will let the managers present instead
She will avoid using any statistics
items.why: Inferência: ela contrapõe precisão a conforto — prefere o dado exato, mesmo desagradável, a tranquilizar o conselho.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's stance in this presentation?
options: Defensive and eager to avoid blame
Direct about the problem yet constructive about next steps
Vague and non-committal about the findings
items.why: Inferência: ela nomeia a disparidade sem suavizar, mas propõe transparência, responsabilização e revisão em 12 meses.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The audit revealed a clear disparity in promotion rates between the two groups." A disparity is…
items.why: Disparity = disparidade: uma diferença ou desigualdade perceptível.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We cannot rely on good intentions; we need ___ before we act."
items.why: Statistical evidence = evidência estatística, o oposto de agir só por boa intenção.

items.q: "Real change is led by the line manager, not by a central initiative." A line manager is…
options: the person who directly manages a team day to day
items.why: Line manager = gestor(a) direto(a), quem chefia a equipe no dia a dia.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "Our data points to ___ to opportunity — some groups simply aren't offered the visible projects."
items.why: Unequal access = acesso desigual: o que impede alguns grupos de chegarem às mesmas oportunidades.

items.q: "Compliance is only a compliance floor — it sets the minimum, not the ambition." This term refers to…
options: a penalty for breaking the rules
the minimum standard the rules require
the highest goal an organisation can reach
items.why: Compliance floor = patamar mínimo: o piso que a regra exige, nunca o teto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas difíceis sobre equidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Two board members pushed back on publishing the figures internally." They…
options: asked for it to be published sooner
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The board agreed to hold managers accountable, but we need to make sure they follow through." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A one-off training day won't move the needle on a gap this size." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on releasing the audit to the whole company." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We keep raising equity in reviews, but it's easy to lose sight of it once targets take over." To lose sight of something means to…
items.why: Lose sight of = perder de vista, deixar de dar atenção a algo em meio a outras prioridades.
